Representation can strongly affect this resource. A [[Sparse Matrix]] avoids storing every zero in a large matrix and instead records the positions and values of its comparatively few nonzero entries.

3110.content:
A source code repository records versioned application files and provides the revision consumed by the continuous-integration pipeline. A pushed change can serve as the trigger and gives the resulting build an identifiable source state.

The repository is the pipeline's starting contract: build definitions, application code, tests, and relevant deployment scripts must agree at that revision. Generated artifacts are outputs and should not obscure which source produced them.

3113.title: Sound Wave Frequency
3113.heading: Sound Wave Frequency
3113.content:
Sound wave frequency is the number of waveform cycles that occur per second, measured in hertz. It is perceived primarily as pitch: faster oscillation generally sounds higher and slower oscillation lower.

Digital game audio represents a complex sound as sampled changes in air pressure containing many frequency components. Playback systems can modify or filter those components through digital signal processing.

3116.sourceSearchName: sound wave amplitude sound wave amplitude
3116.title: Sound Wave Amplitude
3116.heading: Sound Wave Amplitude
3116.content:
Sound wave amplitude describes the magnitude of pressure variation in a waveform and is associated with perceived loudness. Digital samples record amplitude at successive moments.

Playback gain scales the signal, while distance attenuation and occlusion can reduce the effective level reaching the listener. Excessive amplitude can exceed the available range and distort through clipping.

3119.title: Sound Texture
3119.heading: Sound Texture
3119.content:
Sound texture is the background layer of audio that shapes the player's immediate relationship to a game world. Adding, removing, muffling, or foregrounding a layer can change tension and focus without conveying a discrete message.

A tune that stops when movement stops can turn silence into suspense. Muting the score while movement sounds become prominent can instead emphasize embodiment, speed, or a state of [[Flow]].

3121.heading: Document

3122.sourceSearchName: sound occlusion and obstruction sound occlusion and obstruction
3122.title: Sound Occlusion and Obstruction
3122.heading: Sound Occlusion and Obstruction
3122.content:
Sound obstruction occurs when geometry blocks the direct path between an emitter and listener but reflected paths remain, while occlusion more completely encloses or isolates the source. Games approximate these conditions with ray casts and changes to volume or frequency content.

The distinction lets an audio system produce different effects for a pillar between two points and a sound sealed behind a wall. Exact acoustic simulation is usually replaced by efficient perceptual cues.

3125.title: Sound Event Handle
3125.heading: Sound Event Handle
3125.content:
A sound event handle identifies one live instance of a [[Game Audio Event]]. Through the handle, game code can pause, stop, reposition, change parameters, or query playback without owning the middleware object's raw lifetime directly.

The handle becomes invalid when playback completes or the instance is released. A sound wrapper should check validity so delayed gameplay code does not manipulate an event that the audio system has already removed.

3128.title: Sort Key
3128.heading: Sort Key
3128.content:
A sort key is the feature or combination of features used to compare [[Data Record|records]] and determine their order. The key must provide an ordering that the [[Sorting Algorithm]] can apply.

A key may be atomic, such as one identifier treated as a single value, or composite, such as sender followed by delivery date. Composite keys order tied values from an earlier field by consulting the next field.

3130.title: Solving Quadratics by Factoring
3130.heading: Document

3131.sourceSearchName: solving quadratics by factoring solving quadratics by factoring
3131.title: Solving Quadratics by Factoring
3131.heading: Solving Quadratics by Factoring
3131.content:
Solving a quadratic by factoring first rewrites the equation in standard form, factors the polynomial, and applies the [[Zero Product Property]]. For example,

$$x^2+2x-3=0$$

factors as ((x+3)(x-1)=0), so (x=-3) or (x=1).

The method is efficient for a [[Factorable Quadratic]], but it depends on setting the product equal to zero. Factoring an expression without first moving all terms to one side does not directly create the separate linear equations.

3132.sourceSearchName: solving quadratics by factoring solving quadratics by factoring
3132.title: Solving Quadratics by Factoring
3132.heading: References

3134.title: Sorting Algorithm
3134.heading: Sorting Algorithm
3134.content:
A sorting algorithm rearranges a collection of [[Data Record|records]] into an order determined by a [[Sort Key]]. Its output must be a [[Permutation]] of the input: every original record is retained, with only the order changed.

Different algorithms offer different advantages. [[Insertion Sort]] accepts streamed input, [[Radix Sort]] distributes records by key parts, [[Quicksort]] is fast in typical in-memory use, and [[Merge Sort]] supports systematic division and parallel work.

3137.title: Sonification
3137.heading: Sonification
3137.content:
Sonification is the process of turning information into sound. It is the auditory counterpart of visualizing data.

A mapping assigns data properties to audible properties such as pitch, intensity, timing, or spatial location. For example, moving a hand through a fluid-flow dataset could produce sounds whose frequencies vary with flow speed. This lets an [[Auditory Display]] communicate patterns without requiring continuous visual attention.

The mapping must remain understandable and should complement rather than overload other information channels.

3140.sourceSearchName: solving an equation solving an equation
3140.title: Solving an Equation
3140.heading: Solving an Equation
3140.content:
Solving an equation is the process of finding every value that makes the equation true. The usual method transforms the original into simpler [[Equivalent Equations]] until the [[Unknown Variable]] is isolated or the possible factors are exposed.

Each transformation must preserve equality and account for restrictions. Linear equations use inverse operations on both sides, while quadratic equations may use factorization, completing the square, or the quadratic formula. The final values are checked by [[Substitution]] into the original equation because intermediate operations can conceal invalid candidates.

3143.title: Solutions of a Quadratic Equation
3143.heading: Solutions of a Quadratic Equation
3143.content:
The solutions of a quadratic equation are the values that make its two sides equal. A factorable equation such as

$$x^2-x=0$$

becomes (x(x-1)=0), giving the two solutions (x=0) and (x=1).

A quadratic may have two distinct real solutions, one repeated real solution, or no real solution. Each candidate is checked by [[Substitution]] into the original equation, especially when the equation originally contained denominators or was transformed from another form.

3146.title: Solvable Group
3146.heading: Solvable Group
3146.content:
A solvable group has a chain from the identity subgroup to the whole group in which each subgroup is normal in the next and each successive quotient is abelian. Abelian groups are therefore solvable.

The symmetric group Sₙ is not solvable for n at least five.

3149.content:
A polynomial is solvable by radicals when its root field lies inside an extension obtained through successive adjunctions of radical elements. Quadratic formulas provide the familiar degree-two case.

The book connects this property exactly to solvability of the polynomial's Galois group.

3152.content: The solution space contains the steps, models, software structures, and technical choices proposed to move from the current state to the desired state in the [[Problem Space]]. Separating the two spaces prevents an early implementation idea from being treated as an immutable requirement and allows several possible solutions to be evaluated against the same business problem.

3155.title: Solution Set of an Inequality
3155.heading: Solution Set of an Inequality
3155.content:
The solution set of an inequality is the collection of all values that make the comparison true. For (x<3), every real number less than three belongs to the solution set, while three itself does not.

The set can be represented verbally, with an [[Interval]], or by [[Graphing Linear Inequalities]] on a number line. Boundary inclusion follows the symbol: (<) and (>) exclude an endpoint, while (\leq) and (\geq) include it. Substitution of a test value can verify the direction and detect sign mistakes.

3158.heading: Solution of an Equation
3158.content:
A solution of an equation is a value for the [[Unknown Variable]] that makes both sides equal when substituted into the original equation. An equation may have one solution, several solutions, no solution, or be an identity with every permitted value as a solution.

A proposed result is not complete until its domain restrictions are respected. Multiplying, dividing, factoring, or cross multiplying can hide excluded values or introduce candidates that do not satisfy the original form. [[Equation Verification]] distinguishes valid solutions from such extraneous candidates.

Solid-state electronics controls current within a solid material rather than through moving mechanical contacts or electrons in a vacuum. Transistors and integrated circuits made switching smaller, cooler, more reliable, and easier to mass-produce.

The transition was not an immediate substitution. Materials theory, purification, fabrication, and circuit design had to mature before solid-state computers surpassed tube-based designs.

3167.content:
At an ideal solid-fluid interface, the coupled model enforces a common temperature and balances heat flux leaving one side with heat flux entering the other. This closes the energy exchange without inventing an arbitrary intermediate boundary temperature.

Contact resistance or an imperfect interface can modify that relationship and create a temperature jump. Geometry repair and [[COMSOL Domain and Boundary Selections|boundary selection]] must preserve the intended shared surface, because disconnected or duplicated boundaries can silently break the coupling.

3170.heading: Solid Oxide Fuel Cell

Oxygen-side ions travel through the ceramic and react with hydrogen or carbon monoxide at the fuel electrode. The source describes high-temperature operation and use in industrial or cogeneration plants, where usable exhaust heat can complement the electrical output. It contrasts with low-temperature polymer-membrane cells.

3173.heading: SOLID Design Principles
3173.content: SOLID names five object-oriented design principles: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, and dependency inversion. Together they ask whether a component has a coherent reason to change, can be extended through a stable boundary, honors the contract of a type it replaces, exposes only relevant capabilities, and depends on abstractions rather than volatile details. 3188.title: Solar Radiation Threat to GPS
3188.heading: Solar Radiation Threat to GPS
3188.content: Solar activity threatens GPS through both spacecraft exposure and signal propagation. The satellites operate in a radiation environment that can damage electronics, while sunspot cycles and coronal mass ejections disturb the ionosphere through which their signals travel. Monitoring spacecraft and space weather permits protective action and warning, but the intensity and timing of major events remain uncertain. Resilience therefore requires hardened hardware as well as models of atmospheric delay.

3191.title: Solar Radiation Geometry
3191.heading: Solar Radiation Geometry
3191.content: Solar-radiation geometry relates a site's latitude, time-of-day hour angle, and seasonal declination to the Sun's altitude, zenith, and azimuth. These angles set how much [[Beam Solar Radiation]] falls on a horizontal or tilted surface. The source uses them to estimate inclined-collector irradiation and to guide fixed tilt or tracking, while clouds and atmospheric attenuation remain separate influences.

3194.title: Solar Photoelectrolysis
3194.heading: Solar Photoelectrolysis
3194.content: Solar photoelectrolysis illuminates electrodes that decompose water, liberating hydrogen and oxygen at opposite electrodes. The source presents it as a solar-driven alternative to supplying all splitting energy from an ordinary external electrical source. Output follows available sunlight, so timing and collection conditions matter. It is distinct from [[Solar Biophotolysis]], which uses living algae rather than illuminated electrode reactions.

3197.title: Solar Pond
3197.heading: Solar Pond
3197.content: A solar pond uses a vertical salt-concentration gradient to keep warm dense water at the bottom instead of letting it circulate to the cooler surface. Its middle nonconvective layer suppresses heat loss while the bottom layer stores solar heat. Hot lower water can drive an organic-fluid power cycle or provide process heat, and cool upper water can serve the condenser. The pond is both collector and storage medium.

3199.sourceSearchName: solar panel tilt solar panel tilt
3199.title: Solar Panel Tilt
3199.heading: Document

3200.sourceSearchName: solar panel tilt solar panel tilt
3200.title: Solar Panel Tilt
3200.heading: Solar Panel Tilt
3200.content: Solar panel tilt sets the angle at which a fixed [[Solar Array]] receives sunlight. The source chooses it with site latitude in mind and adjusts it toward the time of highest load or desired seasonal collection. Changing tilt changes incident beam radiation, so array capacity cannot be judged separately from orientation and local solar geometry. A tracker is an alternative to a fixed panel.

3201.title: Solar Panel Tilt

3203.title: Solar Module
3203.heading: Solar Module
3203.content: A solar module connects several [[Solar Cell]]s in a series-parallel wiring arrangement and encloses them under a rigid transparent cover. The number of cells in series helps set voltage, while parallel paths increase current. Contacts, cover, frame, and exposed gaps distinguish module performance from that of an individual cell. Modules are the repeatable building blocks of a [[Solar Array]].

3206.title: Solar Constant
3206.heading: Solar Constant
3206.content: The solar constant is the mean intensity of the Sun's beam measured normal to its direction just outside Earth's atmosphere. The source uses approximately 1.353 kW per square meter and notes a yearly variation from Earth's changing distance to the Sun. It is an incoming extraterrestrial reference, not the guaranteed radiation at a collector after clouds and atmospheric absorption.

3208.sourceSearchName: solar concentration ratio solar concentration ratio
3208.title: Solar Concentration Ratio
3208.heading: Document

3209.sourceSearchName: solar concentration ratio solar concentration ratio
3209.title: Solar Concentration Ratio
3209.heading: Solar Concentration Ratio
3209.content: Concentration ratio is a focusing collector's receiving aperture area divided by its absorber or receiver area. A larger ratio can produce a more intense beam and higher useful fluid temperature at the smaller receiver. The source contrasts line-focus parabolic troughs with point-focus dishes and heliostat fields. Ratio alone is not delivered heat: mirror reflection, interception, absorption, and receiver losses also count.

3210.sourceSearchName: solar concentration ratio solar concentration ratio
3210.title: Solar Concentration Ratio
3210.heading: References

3212.title: Solar Collector
3212.heading: Solar Collector
3212.content: A solar collector absorbs incident sunlight and transfers useful heat to a fluid such as water or air. Heat can serve a task directly or feed a later power cycle. The source groups collectors by operating temperature and distinguishes flat-plate units, which can use diffuse light, from focusing units that concentrate [[Beam Solar Radiation]]. Useful heat is incident absorbed energy minus optical and thermal losses.

3215.filePath: 6 - Full Notes/Solar Collector Heat Removal Factor.md
3215.title: Solar Collector Heat Removal Factor
3215.heading: Solar Collector Heat Removal Factor
3215.content: The heat removal factor describes how effectively a collector's fluid extracts energy from its heated absorber. The source multiplies both absorbed-radiation gain and heat-loss terms by this factor in a [[Flat-Plate Solar Collector]] useful-heat equation. It depends on flow and collector design, so a coating's optical absorption alone does not determine delivered heat. Collector performance curves combine it with optical efficiency and heat-loss coefficient.

3218.title: Solar Collector Exergy Efficiency
3218.heading: Solar Collector Exergy Efficiency
3218.content: Solar-collector exergy efficiency compares the exergy gained by its heated fluid with the exergy carried by incident sunlight. The source calculates useful gain from fluid mass flow and specific exergy increase. This can be much lower than the collector's heat-energy efficiency, especially for low-temperature output. The distinction helps choose between a [[Flat-Plate Solar Collector]] for heating and a concentrated receiver for high-grade power tasks.

3221.title: Solar Clearness Index
3221.heading: Solar Clearness Index
3221.content: The clearness index compares radiation measured on a horizontal ground surface over a period with extraterrestrial radiation expected for that same period. It groups atmospheric absorption, scattering, sun angle, and cloudiness into one ratio. The period may be hourly, daily, or monthly; a design calculation must use the matching timescale. A low index signals little usable site radiation despite the [[Solar Constant]].

3224.heading: Solar Chimney Power Plant
3224.content: A solar chimney plant heats ground-level air beneath a transparent cover. Warm air rises through a tall chimney because of its density difference from cooler air, and the resulting flow drives an air turbine and generator. The source calls this semi-direct: sunlight creates the air flow, but a moving turbine still converts its mechanical energy into electricity. Chimney height and collecting area affect output.

3227.heading: Solar Central Receiver
3227.content: A central receiver intercepts the concentrated beams of a [[Solar Tower Power Plant]] and transfers their energy through absorber surfaces to a heat-transfer fluid. The source describes tube panels with headers, allowing high flux and thermal expansion. Rays that miss the target, reflection, wind convection, thermal radiation, and conduction to supports subtract from useful heat even when the heliostat field aims correctly.

3230.title: Solar Cell
3230.heading: Solar Cell
3230.content: A solar cell is an individual semiconductor device that uses a [[P-N Junction]] to deliver electrical power from incident sunlight. Light generates carriers in the junction, while contacts take the resulting current to an external circuit. Cells have material-dependent voltage and illumination- and area-dependent current. They can be wired into a [[Solar Module]] for higher useful voltage or current.

3232.sourceSearchName: solar cell fill factor solar cell fill factor
3232.title: Solar Cell Fill Factor
3232.heading: Document

3233.sourceSearchName: solar cell fill factor solar cell fill factor
3233.title: Solar Cell Fill Factor
3233.heading: Solar Cell Fill Factor
3233.content: Fill factor compares a cell's real maximum electrical power with the rectangle formed by its open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current: $FF=P_{max}/(V_{oc}I_{sc})$. A better-shaped [[Solar Cell Current-Voltage Curve]] has a larger factor. The source uses it in estimating $P_{max}$, so the two endpoint measurements alone are not enough to determine deliverable peak power.

3236.title: Solar Cell Maximum Power Point
3236.heading: Solar Cell Maximum Power Point
3236.content: The maximum power point is the voltage-current combination on a [[Solar Cell Current-Voltage Curve]] for which $P=VI$ is greatest. It is not the open-circuit or short-circuit endpoint, because power at either endpoint is zero. The source obtains it by plotting power against voltage or current; its coordinates provide the usable peak rating for a cell or module under stated radiation.

3239.title: Solar Cell Current-Voltage Curve
3239.heading: Solar Cell Current-Voltage Curve
3239.content: A solar-cell current-voltage curve records how output current changes as operating voltage changes under a particular illumination level. It marks open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current, and an interior operating point where their product is greatest. Comparing curves at different radiation levels shows why the available electrical output of a [[Solar Cell]] changes with sunlight. See [[Solar Cell Maximum Power Point]].

3242.title: Solar Biophotolysis
3242.heading: Solar Biophotolysis
3242.content: Biophotolysis is a sunlight-and-water hydrogen-production route that uses the ability of green algae to release hydrogen. The source specifies an oxygen-free, sulfur-free environment for its example. The biological reactor's light, growth, and gas-handling conditions distinguish it from electrode-based [[Solar Photoelectrolysis]]. It is a proposed production method, not a way for hydrogen to appear without solar input.

3245.title: Solar Array
3245.heading: Solar Array
3245.content: A solar array interconnects [[Solar Module]]s to supply a chosen voltage, current, and power. Series-connected modules raise operating voltage; parallel-connected branches increase output current. The source sizes these counts from nominal module ratings and required generator voltage and current. Array output also reflects mismatch, wiring, temperature, and the fraction of total exposed area actually covered by cells.

3250.sourceSearchName: software world inhabitants software world inhabitants
3250.title: Software World Inhabitants
3250.heading: Software World Inhabitants
3250.content:
An inhabitant is a user engaged in the virtual world created by software. During use, the world’s objects and rules become the practical environment through which the person acts.

Thinking of users as inhabitants draws attention to learned practices, expectations, social relationships, and breakdowns. It discourages treating people as external inputs to an otherwise self-contained technical system.

3253.title: Solar Air Mass
3253.heading: Solar Air Mass
3253.content: Air mass compares the atmospheric path length traversed by a sunlight beam with the path when the Sun is directly overhead. For ordinary solar zenith angles, the source uses $AM=1/\cos\theta_z$; it is one at sea-level zenith and grows as the Sun lowers. A longer path generally increases atmospheric attenuation, helping explain changing radiation and photon flux at a site.

3255.title: Software Satisfaction Ladder
3255.heading: Document

3256.sourceSearchName: software satisfaction ladder software satisfaction ladder
3256.title: Software Satisfaction Ladder
3256.heading: Software Satisfaction Ladder
3256.content:
The software satisfaction ladder ranges from no trust through cynical use, promise fulfillment, environmental fit, avoidance of negative consequences, and delight. Each level demands broader attention to the customer’s experience and future.

Ascending the ladder expands design from basic correctness toward practices, breakdowns, and evolving concerns. Higher levels cannot be specified entirely in advance because they depend on relationships between producers, users, and changing contexts.

3258.heading: Document

3259.title: Software Process Feature
3259.heading: Software Process Feature
3259.content:
A software process feature summarizes how code has been developed or changed. Commit frequency, developer activity, prior defects, ownership, and churn are examples.

Process measures can reveal risk that static code metrics miss because unstable history and coordination matter. Their calculation requires a clear time window and careful identity and repository cleaning.

3262.sourceSearchName: software environmental fit software environmental fit
3262.title: Software Environmental Fit
3262.heading: Software Environmental Fit
3262.content:
Software achieves environmental fit when it aligns seamlessly with established practices and social norms. Users can incorporate it into their work without reconstructing their entire way of acting.

An ATM illustrates the principle by preserving familiar banking transactions in a new interface. Fit turns functional capability into practical usefulness by respecting the environment in which the capability is exercised.

3263.sourceSearchName: software environmental fit software environmental fit
3263.title: Software Environmental Fit
3263.heading: References

3265.title: Software Development
3265.heading: Software Development
3265.content:
A set of computer science activities that are dedicated to the process of creating, designing, and supporting [[Software]].

For interactive software, [[User Interface]] design is part of the development process rather than a cosmetic step at the end. [[Usability Engineering]] iterates through analysis, design, implementation, and [[User Interface Evaluation]] so evidence from a [[Prototype]] can refine the system before it is treated as complete.

3268.title: Software Design Principles Patterns and Hints
3268.heading: Software Design Principles Patterns and Hints
3268.content:
Software designers draw on principles, patterns, and hints at different levels of generality. Principles guide choices toward system qualities, patterns describe recurring situations and proven structures, and hints capture judgments learned through experience.

None of the three is a mechanical recipe. Their value depends on recognizing when a situation fits, understanding the tradeoffs, and adapting the guidance to the system’s users, risks, and constraints.

3271.title: Software Delight
3271.heading: Software Delight
3271.content:
Software delight occurs when a product creates valuable possibilities beyond what users expected. It reflects a producer’s understanding of the customer’s world and can inspire strong loyalty and advocacy.

Delight is contextual and temporary. Once a capability becomes familiar, expectations rise, so sustaining it requires continuing attention to changing practices rather than a one-time feature.

3274.title: Software Crisis
3274.heading: Software Crisis
3274.content:
The software crisis named the recurring pattern of projects delivered late, over budget, unreliable, unsafe, or not delivered at all. As programs grew into products, techniques for individual programmers could not manage their complexity and long operational lives.

The NATO conferences of 1968 and 1969 promoted software engineering as a response. The crisis shifted attention from merely producing code to creating dependable systems through disciplined design, testing, organization, and maintenance.

3276.sourceSearchName: software change entropy software change entropy

3277.sourceSearchName: software change entropy software change entropy
3277.title: Software Change Entropy
3277.heading: Software Change Entropy
3277.content:
Software change entropy measures how a change is distributed across files or components. Concentrated edits have lower entropy, while broadly scattered edits have higher entropy.

The feature represents diffusion rather than raw change size. A change touching many areas unevenly can therefore differ from one of similar size concentrated in a single component.

3280.heading: Software Code Feature
3280.content:
A software code feature measures static properties of a software artifact, such as size, complexity, coupling, or organization. These product metrics summarize what the code is like at a selected revision.

Code features are interpretable and widely available, but they provide only a snapshot. Combining them with process features captures how the artifact reached that state.

3283.heading: Software as Equal to Hardware
3283.content:
A general-purpose computer can perform radically different work only through the procedures that direct it. This gives software a status equal to hardware, unlike a classical machine whose operating procedure is tied to one physical purpose.

Early designers underestimated the effort required to create and maintain programs. As applications expanded, programming languages, operating systems, and reusable libraries became major technologies in their own right.

3286.heading: Software as a Virtual World
3286.content:
Software creates a virtual world in which users perceive objects, take actions, follow rules, and pursue purposes. Games make this structure explicit, but spreadsheets, marketplaces, social networks, and service apps also define distinctive worlds.

Designing the world means shaping possible actions, norms, feedback, and identities—not just implementing functions. A useful system lets its inhabitants accomplish meaningful work within a coherent experience.

3289.heading: Software as a Service
3289.content:
Software as a service delivers a hosted application that performs a recognizable function for its users. The consumer uses the application without installing, updating, or directly managing the operating system and infrastructure beneath it.

Examples include customer relationship management, billing, communication, office productivity, and rendering tools. SaaS can lower local maintenance and support needs, but availability, data protection, provider dependency, export formats, and backup remain consumer concerns.

3292.title: Software Analytics
3292.heading: Software Analytics
3292.content:
Software analytics applies data analysis and learning to artifacts created during software development and operation. Source code, commits, defects, crashes, reports, and developer activity provide different feature spaces.

Feature engineering connects these heterogeneous records to prediction targets. Useful representations combine product structure with development process, time, change diffusion, and natural-language evidence.

3294.heading: Document

3295.sourceSearchName: software architecture mirrors organizations software architecture mirrors organizations
3295.title: Software Architecture Mirrors Organizations
3295.heading: Software Architecture Mirrors Organizations
3295.content:
A software system tends to reflect the communication structure of the organization that builds it. Teams that coordinate through particular boundaries often produce components and interfaces with similar boundaries.

This relationship can be used deliberately by aligning team responsibilities with a desired architecture. If ignored, organizational silos may become accidental technical dependencies that make integration and change harder.

3298.title: Softmax Function
3298.heading: Softmax Function
3298.content:
The softmax function converts a vector of real-valued outputs into a probability distribution. Every resulting value lies between zero and one, and all values sum to one.

In a multiclass [[Classifier]], each output corresponds to one label and can be interpreted as the network's confidence for that class. [[Categorical Cross-Entropy]] compares this predicted distribution with the target distribution during training.

3301.sourceSearchName: soft margin support vector classification soft margin support vector classification
3301.title: Soft-Margin Support Vector Classification
3301.heading: Soft-Margin Support Vector Classification
3301.content:
Soft-margin support vector classification introduces nonnegative slack variables for observations that enter the margin or cross the separating boundary. The objective balances a wide margin against the total penalty for these violations.

The regularization constant controls this tradeoff. A large penalty prioritizes training fit, while a smaller penalty tolerates more violations to obtain a smoother boundary that may generalize better when labels overlap or contain noise.

3304.sourceSearchName: soft body cloth collision soft body cloth collision
3304.title: Soft-Body Cloth Collision
3304.heading: Soft-Body Cloth Collision
3304.content: A pliable object should deform as forces act on it rather than behave like an unyielding fragment. The book demonstrates this by holding the top edge of a textured plane and animating a sphere into and away from it as a collider. The cloth simulation supplies the resulting bend and rebound without hand-keyframing every fold. Soft-body dynamics suit flags, fabric, and other compliant forms; complex liquid or gas interaction calls for [[Fluid Simulation of Splashes and Fire]].

3307.title: Soft Evidence
3307.heading: Soft Evidence
3307.content:
Soft evidence supplies a probability distribution over a variable's possible values rather than asserting one observed value with certainty. It represents an uncertain measurement, an upstream inference, or another source whose output remains probabilistic.

A coherence variable can connect a mirror variable carrying that distribution to the corresponding variable in the target model. This preserves both the original prior and the uncertainty of the new evidence without pretending the distribution is a single value.

3310.heading: Soft Authentication Token
3310.content:
A soft authentication token is a software-generated credential used to demonstrate possession of an enrolled device or secret. It commonly produces a time-limited or challenge-based value that supplements [[Password Authentication]].

As a possession factor in [[Multi-Factor Authentication]], it can prevent a password alone from granting access. Its protection still depends on device security, enrollment integrity, recovery procedures, and resistance to real-time interception.

3313.title: Societal Cloud
3313.heading: Societal Cloud
3313.content:
A societal cloud serves people connected by a common geography, language, institution, hobby, industry, or civic interest. It can provide shared communication, documents, information, analysis, or services within that community boundary.

Aggregated and de-identified data can support group-level analysis, while the service can broker more individualized capabilities for members. The shared purpose must not be treated as blanket permission to expose personal information.

3316.heading: Social Virtual Assistant
3316.content:
A social virtual assistant is designed to participate in relationship-oriented interaction as well as complete instrumental tasks. It uses conversational style, memory, and an [[Assistant Personality]] to create continuity across encounters.

Social behavior can improve engagement, but apparent empathy or companionship may encourage users to attribute abilities the system does not possess. Design should keep the assistant's actual limits legible.

3319.title: Social Robot
3319.heading: Social Robot
3319.content:
A social robot is an embodied system that interacts with people through speech, movement, gaze, expression, and spatial behavior. Its physical presence makes [[Nonverbal Communication]] part of the interface.

Unlike a screen-only assistant, it must locate speakers, orient sensors, coordinate motion with dialog, and behave safely in shared space. Embodiment intensifies both social expectations and technical failure modes.

3322.title: Social Recommendation
3322.heading: Social Recommendation
3322.content:
Social recommendation augments a recommender system with relationships or interactions among users. Friendship, following, trust, membership, and communication can add evidence beyond a person's direct history with items.

A useful model distinguishes [[Individual Preference]] for content from [[Interpersonal Influence]] exerted by senders. Combining them explains why the same item may be adopted by one receiver and rejected by another.

3325.title: Social Phishing
3325.heading: Social Phishing
3325.content:
Social phishing personalizes a deceptive message with information drawn from social profiles, relationships, or recent activity. Familiar names and plausible context make the request appear more credible than a generic phishing attempt.

Reducing exposed personal details, warning about unusual requests, authenticating sensitive actions, and detecting compromised accounts limit the value of this contextual targeting.

3328.title: Social Networking Services
3328.heading: Social Networking Services
3328.content:
A social networking service provides a shared online environment for identities, relationships, messages, media, and continuing updates. Its value grows from the interactions and content contributed by participants.

These services descend from bulletin boards, chat rooms, Usenet, and commercial online communities. Centralized platforms combine those functions at scale while controlling access to much of the resulting data.
